It holds no persistence details (no SQL, ORM or storage access), no transport or framework code (no HTTP, request/response or controller logic), and no business rules of its own, because the validation logic lives in the domain entity. Calling crypto.randomUUID() for the ID and new Date() for the timestamp is a small infrastructure concern, but generating IDs inside a use case is a common, accepted application-layer practice, so it is not a misplaced responsibility. No ADR text was given that says otherwise.
